observations.body: Promise precedes law and confinement. Brothers, speaking of human terms, though it is only a man’s covenant, yet when it has been confirmed, no one makes it void or adds to it. But the Scripture imprisoned all things under sin, that the promise by faith in Jesus Christ might be given to those who believe.

payload.posture: Read Galatians 3:15–22 as one movement in Paul's story, keeping the passage's actions, setting, sequence, and limits visible.
payload.tension: The passage states promise precedes law and confinement. Brothers, speaking of human terms, though it is only a man’s covenant, yet when it has been confirmed, no one makes it void or adds to it. But the Scripture imprisoned all things under sin, that the promise by faith in Jesus Christ might be given to those who believe. It does not by itself supply every cause or later interpretation of this part of Paul's story.
